newsitem.title: USA: Financial advisor admits cheating teachers.
newsitem.headline: Financial advisor admits cheating teachers.

text.p: A former financial advisor pleaded guilty Monday to charges that he schemed to defraud New York and Connecticut school teachers out of retirement savings that had been entrusted to him.

Wayne Drinkwine, 44, of Riverhead, N.Y., principal owner of Mutual Financial Services pleaded guilty to 20 counts of mail fraud and two counts of perjury in testimony before the Securities and Exchange Commission.
He faces up to five years in prison and a fine of $250,000 on each of the 22 counts.

Beginning in 1993, Drinkwine had met with teachers in Westchester County and Long Island, N.Y., and in Connecticut while he was working for a company administering retirement plans for school districts, prosecutors said.

He advised the teachers about individual retirement planning and other investments. He also opened brokerage accounts on behalf of the teachers and earned commissions from securities transactions in these accounts.

Beginning in 1990, he encouraged some teachers to put their money in certain real estate investments through his own firm. He guaranteed the investments would generate a 10 percent return without risk to the principal.
Five teachers entrusted more than $500,000, which was the majority of their retirement savings, to Drinkwine.
In addition, in 1992 and again in 1994, Drinkwine received more than $30,000 from three teachers to invest in stocks and annuities he recommended.
Drinkwine admitted during his plea hearing that he did not invest the funds but kept them for himself.
